name: Replit
tagline: Browser IDE with agents, instant apps, hosting, and deployment

pricing.notes: Official pricing page and 2026 updates checked; public page shows Core around $20/month annual-effective and $25/month monthly depending toggle.

tiers.name: Starter
tiers.limits: 1 published project; free daily Agent credits are provided, but the numeric daily amount is not publicly stated.

tiers.name: Core
tiers.limits: $25 in monthly usage credits; 5 collaborators; 2 parallel agents.
tiers.notes: Annual price is the published monthly equivalent.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: $100 in monthly usage credits; 15 collaborators; 50 viewers; 10 parallel agents; 28-day rollback history.
tiers.notes: Annual price is the published monthly equivalent.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom seats, credits, controls, support and contract terms.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 1 published project plus a daily Agent-credit grant whose exact numeric size is not publicly stated
pricing.billingTerms: monthly and annual for Core and Pro; Enterprise custom
pricing.hiddenCosts: Agent work, deployments, compute, storage and other resources draw from the included dollar credit and then become pay as you go; current resource rates can change, and taxes are extra.

verdictSummary: A dev container plus code-server plus deployment can replace some value, but Replit's beginner-friendly cloud IDE, agents, secrets, hosting, and zero-setup environment are a platform.
coreLoopDIY: Run code-server in a cloud VM, add templates, secrets, git, AI coding extension, and one-click deploy scripts.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because code runs in the browser immediately without local environment drama.

priorArt.name: code-server
priorArt.desc: Open-source VS Code in the browser; useful base for a DIY cloud IDE.

alternatives.name: code-server
alternatives.desc: VS Code in a browser; agents, hosting and deployment are separate chores.

facts.install: Install script, OS package or Docker container
facts.dataFormat: Projects, extensions and VS Code settings live on the host or server filesystem
facts.gapVsPaid: It is only the browser IDE layer: agents, managed runtimes, databases, hosting and deployment are separate jobs.
facts.setupBlocker: Remote use requires authentication plus TLS or a reverse proxy, and you maintain the host, storage and updates

alternatives.name: Coder
alternatives.desc: Full cloud workspaces on your infrastructure; Terraform and PostgreSQL come along for the ride.

facts.install: Install the control plane, connect PostgreSQL and define workspaces with Terraform
facts.engines: Coder AI Agents can connect to Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Amazon Bedrock and self-hosted model endpoints
facts.dataFormat: Control-plane state in PostgreSQL; source code and tool state inside provisioned workspace volumes or repositories
facts.gapVsPaid: It is an infrastructure platform for engineering workspaces, not Replit's beginner-friendly instant IDE, agent and app-hosting service.
facts.setupBlocker: Terraform plus your own Docker, VM or Kubernetes infrastructure and a production PostgreSQL deployment

alternatives.name: Eclipse Che
alternatives.desc: A real browser IDE platform, assuming Kubernetes already counts as normal in your house.

facts.install: Install the Che Operator or chectl into an existing Kubernetes or OpenShift cluster
facts.dataFormat: Code and tools run in Kubernetes pods; durable workspace state uses persistent volumes and Devfile or Kubernetes resources
facts.gapVsPaid: It assumes Kubernetes and platform administration, while Replit turns a browser tab into an agent-built and deployed app with almost no infrastructure work.
facts.setupBlocker: A working Kubernetes or OpenShift cluster is required before the IDE can be installed

notes: Good 'kinda' because the core is composable but platform polish matters.
prompt:
Build me a personal cloud dev environment to replace Replit, on a VPS I already have.
Requirements:

- code-server (VS Code in the browser) behind Caddy with HTTPS and basic auth, installed
  by one setup script. This is assembly of good parts, not a new IDE.
- A `dev new <name> --template node|python|static` CLI that copies from a templates/
  folder (each with .gitignore, README stub, and a run script) into ~/projects/<name>
  and runs git init.
- Each project gets a port in projects.json; Caddy routes <name>.dev.mydomain.com to it,
  so anything I run is instantly viewable at a URL.
- `dev deploy <name>` commits and restarts the project's systemd user service; `dev logs
  <name>` tails it.
- Per-project secrets in <project>/.env, never committed; the template .gitignore
  enforces it.
- Nightly tarball of ~/projects to a backups/ folder, keep 7.
- Reachable only over HTTPS with auth (bind to a VPN interface instead if one exists);
  no telemetry.
- Out of scope: multiplayer editing, hosted AI agents, and per-project containers. One
  VPS, one user, my own projects.
- README: the wildcard DNS record, Caddy config, and code-server auth setup.
